rules: Every table uses immutable UUID id and server created_at.
Non-null columns, state sets, positive amounts, date ordering and arithmetic are CHECK/NOT NULL constraints listed per table.
Composite FKs prevent ticket/type/seat/hold/order/staff/payout context mismatches. Optional-FK NULLs use MATCH SIMPLE; guards require context where needed.
One allocation in held/sold/refund_quarantine per non-null event_seat_id, including expired-but-not-yet-closed holds.
Count active allocation states after event mutex. Live held rows count until explicit release; sold and refund_quarantine count. Validate type and event capacity before insert/edit.

Assigned mode requires allocation.event_seat_id; general mode forbids it. Seat is unblocked, mapped to selected type and event. Count configured unblocked seats consistently with event capacity/type limits.
UNIQUE(ticket_order.hold_id), UNIQUE(order_item.allocation_id); item composite FKs enforce same hold/event/type.
UNIQUE(ticket.order_item_id). TX must issue all and only the fulfilled order's items; pending/failed orders have no ticket.
DDL upper bound + TX exact count
Unique fulfillment attempt reference, immutable confirmed_at and guarded pending->confirmed transition. Multiple successful payment attempts permitted; extras compensated.
Selected fulfillment/activation payment must belong to that exact target's intent; status succeeded and amount/currency/environment match. Same-event FK alone is insufficient.
UNIQUE(refund.payment_attempt_id); amount equals actual successful charge. Failures retry the same obligation; unknown outcome reconciles.
Invalidate/quarantine and commit before external request. Only authoritative success releases; compensation for another attempt does not invalidate legitimate order tickets.
Under event+campaign lock: redemption count + active reservation count < max before new allowance; refund leaves redemptions intact. One active reservation per hold and one redemption per order.
Unit sums equal saved order totals; integer rounding and remainder allocation exact. Percent eligible lines only; fixed discount once per order; no stacking.
Partial UNIQUE(ticket_id) WHERE reversed_at IS NULL; unique consumed entry confirmation and device operation key.
Verified claimed attendee, current attendee/scanner sessions, same-event permission, gate/time checks and valid state required. Check-in + token consumption + ticket state + audit are one commit.
Unique reversal per check_in; reversal row and reversed_at update atomically. Do not restore already invalid ticket or reuse consumed proof.
Client IDs intentionally untrusted; validate to resolved FK IDs. Current-state reconciliation can reject stale operations; provisional records never inflate authoritative attendance.
Owner/member/capability and resource relationships checked on every read/write/download/subscribe. Composite FKs do not replace access control. No unrestricted browser/mobile DB access.

Post-quote price/recipient/seat snapshots and historical FKs do not change; creating new order after expiry/rebuy is required. Audit/messages/ledger/redemption/terms changes are rejected by append-only triggers.
DDL trigger for append-only; TX for snapshot guards

After event mutex, subtract pending payouts and every unresolved full refund liability from actual ledger balance. No sandbox/live transfer; successful debit keyed once. Later refund appends adjustment.
Audit/outbox insert in business transaction; remote calls after commit. Leased workers fence acknowledgements; domain idempotency remains after job retries.
All FK deletes/updates RESTRICT. No normal hard-delete domain API. Append-only tables reject UPDATE/DELETE; owner/migration role is outside ordinary application permissions.
Private access is account grant/authorized role. If support includes order and ticket, ticket's item must belong to that order; GA4 connection must belong to event organization.
Clean content before link/download; purpose/MIME/size verified. Encrypt sensitive payout/file/backup data, hash one-time secrets; secrets stay out of logs, audit, jobs and analytics.
UTC instants plus valid named zone; database clock decides expiry, no time-dependent index predicates. Upcoming/active/completed and seat availability are derived.
Event UID unique/stable, sequence increases on material changes. Duplicate creates new UID/IDs and whitelisted configuration only.
Aggregate each grain before joins: order/item, successful payment, successful refund, current admission. Optional GA4 cache never overwrites canonical amounts.

stateMachines.guard: Only active holds transition; closed_at set once. Consumed holds never expire.

stateMachines.states: held -> sold -> refund_quarantine -> released; held -> released; sold -> released for free cancellation
stateMachines.guard: Released is terminal. Partial uniqueness releases seat only in released state.

stateMachines.states: pending -> confirmed | failed | expired | cancelled; confirmed -> refund_pending -> refunded; confirmed -> cancelled for free registration
stateMachines.guard: One fulfillment; failed refund attempt leaves order refund_pending. Late charge on expired order compensates without confirmation.

stateMachines.states: created -> pending -> succeeded | failed; created -> succeeded | failed
stateMachines.guard: Unknown remains pending; verified late contradictory success retained/reconciled. Succeeded never downgraded by stale failure.

stateMachines.states: valid <-> checked_in (authorized reversal); valid/checked_in -> refund_pending -> refunded; valid/checked_in -> cancelled on allowed cancellation
stateMachines.guard: No return from refund_pending/refunded/cancelled to valid. Checked-in voluntary refund needs reversal/review.

stateMachines.states: requested -> pending -> succeeded | failed; failed -> pending; pending/failed -> succeeded on reconciled success
stateMachines.guard: Same logical obligation/request identity; succeeded terminal. Stock stays quarantined until succeeded.

stateMachines.states: incomplete -> pending -> active | failed; failed -> pending; active <-> suspended
stateMachines.guard: Every prerequisite rechecked on activation/reinstatement. Historical activation fee retained.

stateMachines.states: open <-> in_progress <-> waiting_customer -> resolved; resolved -> open on requester reply
stateMachines.guard: Only authorized current participants; every status/assignment transition produces case_change.

stateMachines.states: pending -> leased -> done | pending | dead; expired leased -> pending
stateMachines.guard: Matching lease token required for ack; terminal jobs not silently replayed as new logical operations.
Sent is historical terminal state. Adjustment is a new finance_entry, not state rewrite.

decisions: Prevents mixed-event policies, activation and refund ambiguity. A basket spanning events is separate orders.
No quantity column: three tickets produce three order_item rows, each with one allocation and at most one ticket. UI can aggregate display lines.
event_id, ticket_type_id, allocation_id, order_item_id and purchased snapshots are never repointed after reservation/fulfillment. Refund/rebuy creates new rows.
Store bigint in 1/100 KZT units: KZT 5,000 = 500000. Rates are basis points. No float; integer rounding with documented remainder distribution.
Concrete representation of confirmed exact KZT requirement.
Recipient email/name is saved per unit; ticket.recipient_user_id remains NULL until that email is verified by claimant. Purchase does not require every recipient account to exist yet; admission does.
Proposed recipient/sign-in mechanism retained from requirements.
One event row as concurrency mutex

Every inventory, campaign, fulfillment, admission, refund, payout or event-gate mutation locks the same event row first within the business lock hierarchy. This deliberately favors correctness and simplicity for the academic deployment.
Design choice; benchmark before finer-grained optimization.
State is not a mutable relationship
Lifecycle transitions change status/timestamp fields; historical FKs remain stable. Released allocation no longer blocks the seat but remains linked to old order/ticket.

DDL enforces row checks, FK scope, unique/partial keys and append-only history. Aggregate totals, state transitions, authorization and atomic multi-table writes require the named TX contracts; SQL file does not implement those services.
All FKs use RESTRICT on delete/update. Disable/revoke/cancel rather than deleting business records. Retention purge is an explicit privileged child-first operation outside normal API.
The DB stores uploaded intents separately from accepted check-ins. Reconnect revalidates current session, membership, ticket and event state; expired proof is rejected and must be renewed.
Requirements baseline; no offline global guarantee.
No redundant calendar or analytics truth tables
ICS reads event.calendar_uid/sequence and event data; basic analytics are views over orders/items/redemptions/check-ins/refunds. GA4 cache is explicitly disposable.
Requester plus currently authorized event support staff, or platform admins for organizer/escalated cases; assigned_to does not itself grant access. No unconstrained participant JSON.

JSON only stores versioned snapshots, safe integration payloads, optional cache and outbox parameters. All core business relationships are typed FKs. Historical audit target and untrusted offline IDs are deliberate exceptions.

Record signed append-only effects. Refund after a sent demo payout appends refund/fee-reversal entries, leaving the payout record untouched and allowing a negative balance. No separate duplicated adjustment table needed.
Reference physical schema for PostgreSQL, not application migrations already deployed. Proposed timing/fee/offline defaults remain proposals; this design does not silently approve them.

transactions.title: Register, verify, sign in, reset and revoke
transactions.gate: Normalized unique email; verified active identity required for purchase. Rate limit outside DB; reset/verification token must be unconsumed and unexpired.
transactions.locks: Lock user then affected sessions/account_token rows in sorted ID order.
transactions.writes: INSERT app_user/account_token/auth_session; consume token conditionally; update verification/password hash; revoke old sessions on reset/logout/suspension; INSERT audit and outbox notification intents.
transactions.relations: All session/token rows retain user_id. Replacement tokens are new rows/digests; do not change token purpose.
transactions.failure: Unique email resolves registration race. Reused/expired token rolls back. Never email raw secrets via persistent plaintext outbox: generate a signed-purpose link from stored challenge ID/key at dispatch or protect a one-time secret with encryption.

transactions.title: Organizer creation, staff invite/accept, grants/revocation
transactions.gate: Owner or explicit manage_staff permission; invite email matches verified account. Scanner is an organization member with event-limited capabilities.
transactions.locks: Lock involved users/sessions, organization, member, then event when assigning/revoking event capabilities.
transactions.writes: INSERT organization, organization_member, staff_invitation, event_staff and permission joins; mark invitation accepted/revoked; revoke membership/assignment and publish access-change event.
transactions.relations: Composite event_staff FKs force event and member into the same organization. owner_user_id changes only in explicit ownership-transfer transaction to an active same-org member.
transactions.failure: Never remove the owner through membership revoke. Invitation replay is no-op/error; unauthorized changes roll back. Revoke WebSocket subscriptions and device packages after commit.

transactions.title: Create/configure event, layout, ticket types and capacity
transactions.gate: Authorized event editor. Layout belongs to venue; seat modes cannot change after active allocations. Validate named timezone, seat coordinates and sales/admission/refund windows.
transactions.locks: Lock organization/event, relevant ticket_types and event_seats; serialize with holds and refunds.
transactions.writes: INSERT/UPDATE event, event_seat, ticket_type, event_media; snapshot seat labels on event copy. Reject capacity/type-limit reduction below all held/sold/quarantine allocations. Increment event availability_version when relevant; INSERT audit.
transactions.relations: Template layout graph is venue > layout > section > row > seat. event_seat points to same layout and same-event type; booked identities cannot be repointed.
transactions.failure: Reject blocking/retargeting an allocated seat. Layout/capacity changes that make counts inconsistent roll back completely. Unallocated drafts may be edited; old paid snapshots never change.

transactions.title: Publish, unpublish, update or suspend event
transactions.gate: Publication needs complete event, usable tickets, valid times; platform-only moderation. Paid activation remains an independent gate.
transactions.locks: Lock organization/event; read relevant types/activation under same event mutex.
transactions.writes: UPDATE publication/moderation/time fields; increment calendar_sequence for calendar changes and availability_version for gate changes; INSERT audit and notification/broadcast jobs.
transactions.relations: Existing orders/tickets remain linked. Unpublish stops new sales without automatically invalidating issued admission; suspension blocks new admission/fulfillment.
transactions.failure: No refund implied by suspension/unpublish. New updates cannot erase allocations. Pending successful charges blocked from fulfillment route to compensation.

transactions.title: Create/replace inventory hold and campaign allowance
transactions.gate: Verified signed-in buyer, permitted visible event, active registration/type windows and limits; activated if any originally paid type. Check requested seats/type quantities and promo rules.
transactions.locks: Lock authorization rows, organization/event; types/campaigns sorted; hold/allocations. Capacity queries run only after event lock.
transactions.writes: INSERT checkout_hold and one inventory_allocation per unit (held). If promo: INSERT promo_reservation after counting lifetime redemptions + active reservation rows. Persist server quote in ticket_order/order_item when checkout accepted. Increment availability_version and audit/outbox.
transactions.relations: Each allocation references one hold/type/event; seat nullable only in general mode. Partial unique live-seat index blocks another held/sold/quarantine row. One active promo reservation per hold.
transactions.failure: All-or-nothing basket. On conflict return availability error, no partial seats. Expired active rows must first be closed under the same lock before their capacity can be reused. Never use now() in partial-index predicates.

transactions.title: Expire, abandon or release a hold
transactions.gate: Server expiry or authenticated hold owner; not a consumed hold.
transactions.locks: Lock event then hold, campaign and allocations under the common sorted hierarchy; recheck state/expiry.
transactions.writes: UPDATE hold to expired/released with closed_at; held allocations -> released with reason/time; active promo reservation -> released; bump availability_version; audit/outbox.
transactions.relations: Rows are retained. Order may become expired/cancelled; no issued ticket is created. If a charge later arrives, process TX-09 compensation.
transactions.failure: If fulfillment already consumed hold, expiry is a no-op. A delayed worker never releases sold/quarantine allocations. Job retries are idempotent.

transactions.title: Quote, create order and initialize payment
transactions.gate: Buyer owns live hold; no other order for it. Validate recipient data, quote lifetime, integer prices/discount/fee allocation and current access/activation.
transactions.locks: Lock event, types/campaign, hold, ticket_order; idempotency guard precedes domain locks.
transactions.writes: INSERT ticket_order and one order_item per allocation with immutable price/recipient/seat/policy snapshots. For positive total INSERT payment_intent + payment_attempt + outbox initialization job; zero-total calls TX-08 directly.
transactions.relations: Unique hold_id prevents two orders for one hold. Composite item FK binds allocation to the same hold/type/event. Payment intent has exactly one target (order XOR activation).
transactions.failure: Changed request under same idempotency key fails. Retry returns existing result after reauthorization. Never call provider while holding DB locks; a persisted attempt reconciles a lost initialization response.

transactions.title: Confirm free or correctly paid order and issue tickets
transactions.gate: Hold still valid, gates active, inventory owned, promo still eligible, received amount/currency/environment correct; no prior fulfillment. Zero total needs no payment.
transactions.locks: Lock event and involved campaign/hold/order/allocations/payment rows; all reads use current committed state after lock.
transactions.writes: Paid path records successful attempt; UPDATE order confirmed with chosen fulfillment attempt/time; hold -> consumed; allocations held -> sold; promo reservation -> consumed and INSERT one promo_redemption; INSERT one ticket per item; INSERT finance entries, audit and delivery/analytics/broadcast jobs.
transactions.relations: ticket_order.fulfillment_payment_attempt_id chooses one charge; UNIQUE(order_item_id) gives exactly one canonical ticket per unit when transaction completes. Allocation and order relationships remain stable.
transactions.failure: Any guard failure issues no ticket. A real successful charge cannot be rolled back externally: record it and create compensation refund via TX-09. Transaction rollback retains no partial issuance.

transactions.title: Verified payment inbox, late success and duplicate charge
transactions.gate: Provider authentication verified before accepted inbox; expected target, amount, currency, merchant and environment checked. Browser return URL is not evidence.
transactions.locks: Persist inbox with unique provider event key; processing transaction locks event then domain rows and marks inbox processed atomically.
transactions.writes: INSERT provider_event; record authoritative attempt result. If fulfillment eligible run TX-08. Else retain extra/late success and INSERT refund+outbox compensation. Reconciliation queries provider outside transaction and feeds same handler.
transactions.relations: Do NOT add a unique successful payment per order: two external charges may truly succeed. Only chosen fulfillment FK is unique; each charged attempt may have one logical refund.
transactions.failure: Repeated event with different payload hash is rejected. Out-of-order failure never demotes succeeded payment. Wrong amount/currency never fulfills; escalate/reconcile/refund any captured money safely.

transactions.title: Claim ticket and issue attendee entry confirmation
transactions.gate: Active verified claimant email matches order item recipient; ticket unclaimed or already assigned to same account. Confirmation requires claimed valid ticket and current attendee session.
transactions.locks: Lock user/session then organization/event, ticket/claim/entry confirmation.
transactions.writes: Consume claim token once; SET ticket recipient_user_id/claimed_at without changing order buyer; INSERT short-lived entry_confirmation. Store only digest/key ID; publish no personal info in QR.
transactions.relations: Composite confirmation FK requires attendee_user_id equal ticket.recipient_user_id; session FK binds session to same user. Resending PDF preserves ticket identity.
transactions.failure: Wrong account/expired token rejected. A claimed ticket cannot be reassigned by ordinary flow. Replaced claim is explicitly revoked before inserting new active claim.

transactions.title: Online check-in or manual admission
transactions.gate: Both attendee and scanner authenticated; device owned; current same-event scan permission; event entrance gate open; token purpose correct; confirmation/session unexpired; ticket valid.
transactions.locks: Lock involved users/sessions and organization membership first; then event, ticket, confirmation and check_in rows. Event lock serializes refunds and admission.
transactions.writes: INSERT check_in; consume entry_confirmation; ticket valid -> checked_in; increment event availability_version; INSERT audit/broadcast outbox in same commit.
transactions.relations: One unreversed check_in per ticket through partial unique index. Device+operation ID unique. Entry confirmation may be consumed by only one check_in.
transactions.failure: Second scan sees already-used. Refund winning mutex makes scan fail; scan winning first makes voluntary refund require reversal/review. A duplicate operation returns original result, never a second admission.

transactions.title: Authorized admission reversal
transactions.gate: Explicit reverse_checkin permission; existing current accepted admission; reason required.
transactions.locks: Lock auth/org/event then ticket/check_in.
transactions.writes: INSERT check_in_reversal; set check_in.reversed_at to reversal timestamp; ticket checked_in -> valid unless already invalidated by authorized event cancellation; audit and publish count update.
transactions.relations: Original check_in stays; UNIQUE(check_in_id) allows one reversal. The old confirmation stays consumed; next entry requires fresh confirmation/new check_in.
transactions.failure: Do not restore refunded/cancelled validity. Repeating reversal is idempotent. No deletion of accepted check-in history.

transactions.title: Approve full refund and quarantine inventory
transactions.gate: Full actual charge only; voluntary policy cutoff saved on order; checked-in units must be reviewed/reversed; authorized actor. Compensation can have no tickets.
transactions.locks: Lock authorization, organization/event, order, allocations, payment/refund and tickets under canonical hierarchy.
transactions.writes: INSERT refund requested (unique payment_attempt_id); order -> refund_pending; tickets -> refund_pending invalid; sold allocations -> refund_quarantine; INSERT audit and refund outbox; COMMIT before provider call.
transactions.relations: All old links remain. Compensation refund on unfulfilled duplicate charge must NOT invalidate the legitimate tickets fulfilled by a different attempt.
transactions.failure: Reject amount mismatch/second logical refund. Pending/failed/unknown refund never releases stock. Once invalidated, do not silently restore old ticket on provider failure.

transactions.title: Dispatch/reconcile refund, confirm success, then release stock
transactions.gate: Provider result corresponds to same full-refund obligation/charge; request acceptance is not final success.
transactions.locks: Worker leases outside business TX; finalization locks organization/event, order/allocation/payment/refund/ticket as applicable.
transactions.writes: INSERT/UPDATE refund_attempt; uncertain -> reconcile, failed -> retain quarantine. Success: refund succeeded/time; chosen fulfillment order -> refunded; tickets -> refunded; quarantine allocations -> released/refund_succeeded; append finance entries/refund fee reversal; notifications/audit/outbox; availability_version++.
transactions.relations: Unique refund per charge and finance source-kind keys prevent duplicate financial/release effects. Replacement purchase uses NEW hold/allocation/order_item/ticket referencing the same event_seat.
transactions.failure: Timeout must not start a different logical refund. If callback replay after success, no additional release. Cancelled/closed/suspended event inventory remains unpurchasable despite allocation release.

transactions.title: Cancel free registration or cancel event
transactions.gate: Free-order owner policy/authorized staff, or organizer cancellation permission. Event cancellation overrides ordinary voluntary-refund eligibility.
transactions.locks: Lock organization/event; operate orders/allocations/tickets in stable order. For large event, close event gate first then durable bounded per-order jobs.
transactions.writes: Free order: tickets cancelled, sold allocations released/free_cancel, order cancelled, audit. Event: event cancelled, calendar_sequence/version++, audit and cancellation jobs; workers invalidate/cancel tickets and initiate paid refunds via TX-13.
transactions.relations: The event gate makes every ticket immediately ineffective even if per-ticket materialization is still queued. Historical FKs and accepted check-ins remain.
transactions.failure: Cancellation job retries must resume without duplicate refunds. Pending payments that later succeed compensate, never fulfill. Refund completion cannot republish cancelled event.

transactions.title: Activate paid sales and suspend/reinstate activation
transactions.gate: Same-event terms, same-org verified payout and approved identity; at least one paid type; exact activation fee success. Platform admin for suspension.
transactions.locks: Lock organization/event, activation/intent/attempt and referenced checklist rows.
transactions.writes: INSERT terms_acceptance, verification_record, payout_profile as needed; sales_activation incomplete->pending->active; choose one paid_attempt_id; append activation fee finance entry/audit. Suspension sets status/reason, never deletes payment.
transactions.relations: payment_intent targets activation exclusively; chosen paid attempt must refer to this activation intent (TX guard beyond same-event FK). Duplicated event starts without these relations.
transactions.failure: Incomplete checklist cannot activate. Duplicate external activation charge is retained and compensated; original legitimate activation remains intact. Simulated identity never presented as production KYC.

transactions.title: Campaign create/edit/disable
transactions.gate: Authorized event editor; fixed/percent rules, dates, limit, applicability valid. Lowered limit cannot undercut already consumed/reserved allowance.
transactions.locks: Lock organization/event then campaign and affected reservations.
transactions.writes: INSERT/UPDATE campaign, promo_code, eligibility joins; immutable redemptions untouched; audit and optional availability/quote update.
transactions.relations: Campaign/type/code/reservation composite keys keep same event. Redemptions remain after refund and continue counting toward lifetime max.
transactions.failure: Disabling while a checkout is pending blocks discounted fulfillment; never silently charge more. Old order discount snapshots and attribution are unchanged.

transactions.title: Create support case, message, attach file, assign/resolve/escalate
transactions.gate: Requester owns/accesses linked context; event/order/ticket context must be mutually consistent. Assigned user must have current support/admin permission.
transactions.locks: Lock relevant auth/org/event if event-scoped; then case. For platform case lock requester organization/case.
transactions.writes: INSERT case/message/attachment; INSERT case_change for status/assignment/escalation; reopen on requester reply; INSERT notification/broadcast outbox; assign persisted cursor order (created_at,id).
transactions.relations: Composite FKs align context event; TX checks ticket belongs linked order when both supplied. Participants are derived requester/current support staff/platform escalation, not untrusted client IDs.
transactions.failure: File must be clean and uploader/context authorized. Same client_message_id deduplicates; connection reconnect reads persisted messages. Revoked staff cannot subscribe/download even if formerly assigned.

transactions.title: Store file, generate PDF/manifest and clean failed uploads
transactions.gate: Purpose, content, type/size/count limits and storage owner checked; protected downloads always reauthorize linked business record.
transactions.locks: Reserve stored_file row in short TX; upload/scan/render outside TX; lock metadata/business row to attach.
transactions.writes: INSERT stored_file pending/quarantined; upload object with checksum; mark clean only after validation; INSERT event_media/support_attachment or update ticket.pdf_file_id/offline_package.file_id; cleanup orphan objects asynchronously.
transactions.relations: DB stores object_key, not blobs or public URL. Delete object only after references checked; mark metadata deleted instead of cascading business history.
transactions.failure: Remote file writes cannot be rolled back atomically with PostgreSQL; use pending state, idempotent object keys, reconciliation and orphan cleanup. Never expose quarantined content.

transactions.title: Issue offline package and reconcile operation batch
transactions.gate: Scanner session/current assignment valid; package unexpired and same device/event; attendee proof must still satisfy online rules at final acceptance.
transactions.locks: Download under event snapshot read consistency. Reconcile each operation with auth/org/event locks, then ticket/confirmation/check-in; bounded batch, per-operation results.
transactions.writes: INSERT offline_package/file; on upload INSERT offline_operation before resolution; valid check-in calls TX-11, reverse calls TX-12; update result and optionally INSERT sync_conflict; refresh snapshot.
transactions.relations: Untrusted claimed IDs deliberately have no FK so invalid scans can be recorded. resolved_ticket_id and accepted_check_in_id are real FKs. Unique device operation ID survives repeated package upload.
transactions.failure: Same key/different hash rejects. Revoked assignment, expired session/proof/package, cancelled/refunded ticket or duplicate admission -> rejection/conflict, no central admission. Device time never overwrites server order.

transactions.title: Reserve/send/fail demo payout and apply later refund adjustment
transactions.gate: Finance permission; payout environment simulation; same-org verified profile; amount <= ledger balance minus pending payout reservations and refund liabilities. Block unresolved charges.
transactions.locks: Lock organization/event, then pending payout/refund/finance scope; all ledger writers also lock this event.
transactions.writes: INSERT demo_payout pending/eligible reserves amount; successful simulation marks sent and INSERT negative finance_entry payout; failed releases reservation by state. Later refund INSERTs signed refund/fee-reversal entries, possibly negative balance.
transactions.relations: Payout profile scope enforced by composite FK. Unique request key and payout-kind ledger key prevent duplicate send/debit. Sent payout row remains unchanged.
transactions.failure: Retry returns same payout. Concurrent refund cannot bypass balance reservation. A post-payout refund never rewrites old payout as if it did not happen; balance adjustment is new finance history.

transactions.title: Deliver notifications, broadcasts and jobs
transactions.gate: Business transaction already committed. Reauthorize live-event delivery and protected links; delayed failure messages recheck current status.
transactions.locks: Lease short batch of pending outbox rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; commit lease; external work outside transaction; ack with matching lease_token.
transactions.writes: INSERT notification/delivery intents with unique business keys; update attempts/status; outbox pending->leased->done/dead; expired lease -> pending; optional reconnect clients query persisted domain records.
transactions.relations: At-least-once side effects; irreversible domain operations have their own unique keys. Outbox payload contains typed IDs/options, not authority.
transactions.failure: Crash before ack may resend; SMTP exactly-once not promised. Fencing prevents an expired worker overwriting a new lease. Dead jobs remain inspectable and manually replayable.

transactions.title: Moderation and settings
transactions.gate: Current platform-admin grant; whitelisted typed settings; explicit reason.
transactions.locks: Lock target user/session or organization/event according to lock order; settings key updates serialized by advisory lock or SERIALIZABLE transaction.
transactions.writes: INSERT moderation_action/platform_setting_version and audit; update target status; revoke sessions/packages; enqueue relevant notices. Settings latest effective version applies only to new quotes/checklists.
transactions.relations: Historical order/policy/fee snapshots unchanged. Moderation target is exactly one typed FK, not a generic target string.
transactions.failure: Suspension does not secretly cancel/refund. Reject settings below active capacity/security requirements. Reported event visibility/access validated on report insertion.

transactions.title: Duplicate past event
transactions.gate: Authorized access to source and target organization; explicit copy whitelist.
transactions.locks: Read source consistently, lock target organization then create fresh event.
transactions.writes: INSERT fresh draft event, media links to authorized files, ticket types and newly mapped event_seats. Fresh calendar UID, sequence 0, no activation. INSERT audit.
transactions.relations: No copies of holds, allocations, orders, tickets, payment/refund/payout rows, attendees, memberships/assignments, campaigns, support or check-ins. New seat/type IDs remapped to new event.
transactions.failure: Copy is all-or-nothing. Shared physical venue/layout may remain referenced; original event and transactions untouched.

transactions.title: Read operational analytics, export GA4, and calendar
transactions.gate: Event-scoped report permission; private event access for ICS; consent/allowlist for GA4.
transactions.locks: Read-only MVCC snapshots for reports; no event FOR UPDATE for reads. Export job leases separately; short cache update.
transactions.writes: Basic analytics SELECT authoritative data; optional INSERT analytics_export, UPSERT ga4_cache; calendar generated from stable UID/sequence without calendar account access.
transactions.relations: Money joins aggregate per order/attempt/refund before combining with items to avoid multiplication. Ticket counts use allocation/ticket validity, not cumulative historical tickets.
transactions.failure: GA4 outage cannot roll back orders. Missing cache is unavailable, not zero sales. Refund measurements use independent idempotency IDs and omit PII/ticket IDs; ICS cancellation reuses UID.

transactions.title: Privileged retention, backup and restore
transactions.gate: No ordinary destructive business API; retention policy separately approved. Backup includes PostgreSQL and object-storage consistency manifest.
transactions.locks: Operational maintenance window or coordinated snapshot; retention deletes explicit child-first sets, never disable FK checks casually.
transactions.writes: Normal flow revokes/archives/cancels. Maintenance may purge expired auth data and orphan objects under documented policy; retain protected audit/financial history. Restore schema, data, objects then verify checks.
transactions.relations: ON DELETE RESTRICT exposes dependencies; no cascade can wipe orders through deleting an event/user. UUIDs stable across recovery.
transactions.failure: Restore test must reconcile pending provider work before resending. Do not replay stale payout/refund jobs as new operations; preserve idempotency keys and provider inbox.
